message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A masterclass in psychological dread, with iconic imagery and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A brutal, atmospheric descent into grief‑driven terror that redefines the genre. |
| 3 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart, socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine scares. |
| 4 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A haunting psychological thriller about grief and motherhood, with a memorable monster. |
| 5 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Suspense built on silence; a tense, family‑driven survival story. |
| 6 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight horror that turns a Swedish festival into a nightmare. |
| 7 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” trope with a relentless, creeping dread. |
| 8 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A well‑crafted supernatural thriller that spawned a successful franchise. |
| 9 | **The Ring** | 2002 | A modern retelling of a Japanese horror classic, with a creepy videotape that haunts. |
|10 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Low‑budget, found‑footage style that still delivers genuine chills. |
|11 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑commentary on horror tropes that still delivers plenty of scares. |
|12 | **Suspiria** (2018) | 2018 | A visually stunning, unsettling remake of the 1977 classic. |
|13 | **The Witch** | 2015 | A slow‑burn, period horror that builds dread through atmosphere and period detail. |
|14 | **It** | 2017 | A modern adaptation of Stephen King’s novel, with a terrifying clown and strong ensemble cast. |
|15 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | A timeless classic that set the standard for demonic possession films. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want psychological dread, supernatural scares, or something that pushes the boundaries of the genre. Enjoy the chills!
